group.passage: Finding an affordable room is a headache for university students in many cities. In the Dutch town of Deventer, a few students have solved the problem in an unexpected way: they live in a home for older people without paying any rent. In return, each student agrees to spend at least 30 hours a month being a good neighbor to the residents, most of whom are in their eighties and nineties. The idea grew out of a complaint. A student told the head of the home how noisy and run-down his student housing was, and their conversations led to the exchange. In its early years, six students shared the building with about 160 older residents. The students are not nurses or caregivers, and there is only one firm rule: they must never become a nuisance to their neighbors. Otherwise, they are free to come and go as they please. What do the students actually do? They watch sports games with the residents, join their birthday parties and sit with those who are ill. Some have taught their neighbors to send emails, use social media and make video calls. Such ordinary moments matter more than they might seem. Research has linked loneliness among older people to poorer health and earlier death, and the World Health Organization estimates that about one person in six around the world feels lonely. The model has since spread to other countries. In 2018, a nursing home in Sydney began offering four health students free rooms and meals in exchange for 30 hours of company each month. The home deliberately gave them no fixed list of tasks, hoping their visits would feel natural rather than planned. In the United States, three graduate students in Michigan lived among about 40 older residents for nearly two years. Sharing a home across generations is not always easy, however. The Michigan students found that some residents were slow to open up, as many had already said goodbye to a long list of friends. While the students lived there, 15 residents died, including several the students counted as friends. Even so, the young people said the experience taught them lessons about aging that no classroom could.

options.A: Why student housing in Dutch cities has become so expensive.
options.B: The health risks that loneliness poses to older people.
options.C: A way of living that brings students and older people together, with its rewards and difficulties.

options.A: Students may live as they like, as long as they do not disturb the residents.
options.B: Students pay a lower rent in addition to giving their time.
options.C: It was first suggested by residents who felt lonely.

questions.stem: What does “Such ordinary moments” in the third paragraph refer to?

options.B: The few rules that the students must follow.
options.C: The months each student spends in the home.

questions.stem: Why were some residents in Michigan probably slow to open up?

options.B: They were afraid of losing yet another person they cared about.
options.C: They thought the students had come only to study them.
options.D: They had been told to keep their distance from the students.

translation_zh.text:
在許多城市，找到負擔得起的房間是大學生的一大難題。在荷蘭的 Deventer 鎮，幾名學生用意想不到的方式解決了這個問題：他們住在一所長者住宅裡，不用付任何房租。作為交換，每個學生同意每個月花至少 30 小時，當住戶的好鄰居；這些住戶大多是八、九十歲的長者。

這個點子源自一次抱怨。一名學生向這所住宅的院長訴苦，說他住的學生宿舍又吵又破舊，兩人的對話促成了這項交換。計畫初期，有六名學生和大約 160 位長者同住在這棟建築裡。學生不是護理人員，也不是照顧者，只有一條嚴格的規定：絕對不能打擾鄰居。除此之外，他們可以自由來去。

學生實際上做些什麼？他們和住戶一起看球賽、參加住戶的生日派對，也陪伴生病的人。有些人教鄰居寄電子郵件、使用社群媒體、視訊通話。這些平凡的時刻比表面上看起來重要。研究發現，長者的孤獨與較差的健康和較早死亡有關；世界衛生組織估計，全世界大約每六個人就有一人感到孤獨。

這種模式後來傳到了其他國家。2018 年，雪梨一家護理之家開始讓四名健康相關科系的學生免費住宿、用餐，換取每個月 30 小時的陪伴。院方刻意不給他們固定的任務清單，希望探訪是自然而然、而不是排定好的。在美國，密西根州有三名研究生和大約 40 位長者一起住了將近兩年。

不過，跨世代同住並不總是容易。密西根的學生發現，有些住戶遲遲不肯敞開心房，因為許多人早已和一長串朋友道別。學生住在那裡的期間，有 15 位住戶過世，其中幾位是學生視為朋友的人。即使如此，這些年輕人說，這段經驗教給他們關於老化的課，是任何教室都教不來的。

I am not sure I could do it, because it would be very sad to lose neighbors I had become close to.
